role: Append-only crash backup of a workout's GPS fixes, per-tick WorkoutSample rows, barometer samples and wrist-HR markers as per-session JSONL files in the App Group WorkoutBackup/ directory, each line sealed with EncryptionManager like RawRRBackup's points (SealedJSONLines; plain lines without a key queue the workout in PendingEncryptionLedger .workoutTrack, re-sealed by reencryptPendingTracks; older plain files still read), with retrieval for crash recovery, verified per-session discard and purge-all.
types: WorkoutTrackBackup: class (@unchecked Sendable) — the backup store, singleton .shared
WorkoutTrackBackup.Header: struct — sessionId, sport, startDate, createdAt
WorkoutTrackBackup.Recovered: struct — hydrated streams returned to recovery
OrderedBackupRow: protocol — rows strictly rising by backupOrderKey
WorkoutSample: extension — OrderedBackupRow keyed by offsetSec
Int: extension — OrderedBackupRow keyed by self
state: file:<AppGroup>/WorkoutBackup/ directory (:172, created with completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication; recreated by purgeAll)
mem:WorkoutTrackBackup.unlockObservers (NotificationTokens: protectedDataDidBecomeAvailable / didBecomeActive observers, removed in deinit)
mem:WorkoutTrackBackup.notificationCenter (where the unlock and activation observers are added; NotificationCenter.default for init(directory:) and init())
mem:WorkoutTrackBackup.resealQueued (OSAllocatedUnfairLock<Bool>: a re-seal queued and not yet started)
toplevel: Stored properties: directory, FileManager.default, NSLock, unlockObservers (NotificationTokens), serial appendQueue, cursor dictionaries, headerWritten set, ISO-8601 encoder/decoder that write and read non-finite numbers as strings (static nonFiniteStrings). Declares OrderedBackupRow protocol and conforms WorkoutSample (offsetSec) and Int (self) to it. Adds WorkoutSample.finiteValuesOnly and the file-private finiteOrNil helper.

units.does: Copies timestamp, coordinate, altitude, horizontal/vertical accuracy, speed and course out of a CLLocation.
Rebuilds a CLLocation from the persisted fields.
Stored-property initializer: JSONEncoder with ISO-8601 dates that writes non-finite Doubles as the strings "Infinity", "-Infinity" and "NaN" (nonFiniteStrings) instead of throwing.
Stored-property initializer: JSONDecoder with ISO-8601 dates that reads the strings "Infinity", "-Infinity" and "NaN" back as non-finite Doubles (nonFiniteStrings).
Convenience init: the app's backup, in <shared container>/WorkoutBackup (init(directory:)).
Convenience init: calls init(directory:notificationCenter:) with the given directory and NotificationCenter.default, the center the app's stores observe unlock and activation on.

Designated init: keeps notificationCenter for the observers, stores the directory (the shared container's WorkoutBackup/ for the app, a temporary one for tests), creates it if missing (createDirectoryIfNeeded), queues the re-seal of workouts written with plain lines (reencryptPendingTracks), and installs, on that center, the unlock and activation observers that queue it again (observeUnlock).
Removes the unlock and activation observers (unlockObservers.removeAll) from the notificationCenter they were added to.
units.entry: Deallocation of the store (tests' per-folder stores; .shared lives for the process)

units.does: Adds a block observer on the store's notificationCenter (any queue) for UIApplication.protectedDataDidBecomeAvailableNotification and for didBecomeActiveNotification, each calling reencryptPendingTracks on the store (held weakly), and keeps the tokens in unlockObservers.

Creates the backup directory with BackupProtection.appendableClass (completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication) when it does not exist (writes can then continue while the device is locked mid-workout); a failure is logged and swallowed, and later writes into the missing directory fail and return false. Run by init(directory:) and by purgeAll.
Returns directory/<uuid>_workout_header.json for the session.
Returns directory/<uuid>_workout_track.jsonl for the session.
Returns directory/<uuid>_workout_samples.jsonl for the session.
Returns directory/<uuid>_workout_baro.jsonl for the session.
Returns directory/<uuid>_workout_hkhr.jsonl for the session.
Synchronously runs appendIncrementalSerialized on the serial appendQueue and returns whether anything was written.

Writes the header once per launch per session, then appends the new tail of the track, samples, baro and wrist-HR streams (each attempted regardless of the others) starting from the cursors or on-disk line counts; returns true if any write happened.
Returns per-stream counts: the in-memory cursor when known this launch, otherwise the newline count of the stream file plus its set-aside copies on disk.
Counts newline bytes across the stream file and its .corrupted_* siblings; unreadable or missing files contribute 0.

branches.cond: file missing or Data(contentsOf:) fails (attempt returns nil)
branches.effect: contributes 0 (read error logged by attempt); else counts lines

units.does: Under lock, sets the given cursor dictionary entry for the session to count.
Appends items[offset...] as JSONL and on success advances the cursor to items.count; returns false (cursor unchanged) when nothing is new or the write failed.

branches.effect: return false, cursor not advanced so the next tick retries

units.does: For a key-ordered stream, starts after the last written key (or at the disk/cursor offset before any write this launch), appends that tail as JSONL, then advances the count cursor and the last-key cursor.

branches.effect: ?? → start = first index keyed after lastKey; nil → start = offset

units.does: Scans from the end and returns the index of the first row whose backupOrderKey is greater than key (items.count when none).

Atomically writes the plain JSON header (sessionId, sport, startDate, createdAt now) with BackupProtection.appendable (completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication) and records the session in headerWritten; returns false and logs on failure.

branches.effect: logged, returns false; header retried on the next tick because headerWritten stays unset

units.does: Encodes items as newline-delimited lines through encodeLines (each sealed, or plain JSON without a key, the workout then queued for re-encryption), every row or none (encodeLines returns nil on any row that fails, logged there; nothing is written and the caller's cursor stays); writes a new file if none exists, otherwise appends through JSONLinesFile.append, which cuts off a row torn by a kill mid-write first (the launch count counts only complete rows, so that row is in this slice again); a failed append is logged and returns false, and a handle that won't open falls back to a rewrite.

branches.cond: items empty, or a row failed to encode

branches.effect: initial write of the blob; returns its result
log the error, return false (cursor stays, next tick retries)

units.does: If the existing file's bytes can be read, rewrites their complete rows (JSONLinesFile.completeLines, a torn last row dropped) plus the new blob (atomically, through write); otherwise moves the file aside as .corrupted_<epoch> and writes the blob fresh — and when that move fails returns false without writing, so the unreadable rows are not overwritten (the cursor stays and the next tick retries).

branches.effect: write(complete rows + blob), atomically: a kill or full disk mid-write leaves the old file whole
return false, nothing written; else write blob alone

units.does: Moves the stream file to <name>.corrupted_<unix seconds> in the same directory; returns false when the move fails (logged by attempt) and the file is still in place.

Encodes the items with the backup encoder (non-finite numbers as strings, so these rows always encode) through SealedJSONLines.encode with the stored manager when its key is reachable: one newline-terminated line per item, sealed and base64-encoded, or plain JSON for the rest of the slice without a key or once sealing fails. A slice with a plain line is logged at .error and the workout recorded in the .workoutTrack PendingEncryptionLedger before it is returned (so before it is written). When any item throws, logs it at .error and returns nil, so no slice is ever written with a row missing.
Writes the blob to url atomically with BackupProtection.appendable (completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication), replacing the file, returning false and logging on error.
Lists the backup directory and returns the UUIDs parsed from the first 36 characters of every file name containing '_workout_' (headers, streams and set-aside copies).

branches.effect: UUID(prefix 36) (nil if not a UUID); else skipped

units.does: Runs retrieveSerialized on appendQueue so a read cannot interleave with an append.

Decodes the header (nil if missing/unreadable/undecodable — logged via logHeaderlessStreams when stream files exist), then the streams, each empty when absent: track via recoveredTrack (fixes without a finite position or altitude dropped), samples with non-finite values cleared to nil (finiteValuesOnly, rows kept), barometer rows with a non-finite altitude dropped, and wrist-HR offsets; returns Recovered. What it returns therefore encodes with the archive's encoder, which rejects NaN and infinity.

branches.effect: logHeaderlessStreams, return nil (the streams cannot be recovered without the sport/start)

units.does: Decodes the track stream and returns it as CLLocations, leaving out fixes whose latitude, longitude or altitude is not a finite number.
Logs a .warning when any of the session's four stream files exists although its header could not be read.
Decodes the set-aside .corrupted_* copies (sorted by name, oldest first) followed by the live stream file and concatenates the rows.
Lists the stream's directory and returns the URLs of siblings named <stream>.corrupted_*.

branches.effect: ?? [] → no set-aside files (error logged by attempt)

units.does: Reads a JSONL file as UTF-8 and decodes each non-empty line, sealed or plain (SealedJSONLines.open with the stored manager): lines that do not open or decode (a torn write, a sealed line whose key is not on this device) are skipped and counted in one log line. Returns [] when the file is missing or unreadable (the read failure logged by attempt).

branches.cond: file missing or not readable as UTF-8
line does not open or decode

units.does: The session's four stream URLs (track, samples, baro, hkhr) followed by every .corrupted_* copy set aside from them (setAsideFiles).

Unless a re-seal is already queued and not yet started (resealQueued.setIfClear), queues one asynchronously on appendQueue (behind any append, so a stream being recorded is rewritten only between appends, never under one). When it starts it clears resealQueued, so a call made while it runs queues the next; with the key reachable (SealedJSONLines.availableManager) it re-seals every workout pending in the .workoutTrack ledger (resealStreams); without it does nothing, and the next launch, unlock or activation tries again.
units.entry: Queued by init(directory:) and by the protectedDataDidBecomeAvailable / didBecomeActive observers installed by observeUnlock; XCTest

units.does: For the workout's stream files in this folder that exist (streamFiles): none → returns, the id stays queued (its files are in another folder, or discard clears it). Otherwise rewrites each file holding a plain line sealed (SealedJSONLines.resealFile: atomic, BackupProtection.appendable, read back) and clears the .workoutTrack ledger entry only when every file holds no plain line. A read, seal or write failure is logged and leaves the id queued.
Runs discardSerialized on appendQueue (sync), so no append can recreate a stream file or cursor after the session's files are deleted; returns (discardable) whether every file went.

Removes the header first (it is what makes a workout recoverable), then the four stream files and their set-aside copies, through BackupFiles.remove, and forgets the session's cursors and headerWritten marker (forgetCursors) either way. When any file is still on disk, logs at .error and returns false (the workout stays queued for re-encryption); otherwise clears its .workoutTrack ledger entry and returns true.

branches.cond: a file is still on disk

units.does: Under lock, removes the session's track, sample, baro and wrist-HR cursors, both last keys and its headerWritten marker.

On appendQueue: deletes every file of every session that has a '_workout_' file on disk (discardSerialized), logging at .error how many sessions kept a file, then clears every in-memory cursor, last-key and header flag, including those of sessions whose files the caller's sweep already removed, and recreates the WorkoutBackup/ directory with its protection class when it is gone (createDirectoryIfNeeded), so later workouts are backed up again without a relaunch (Delete All My Data).

branches.cond: for each session id on disk
branches.effect: discardSerialized(id); those that keep a file are counted

units.does: WorkoutSample's backup order key is its offsetSec.
A copy of the sample with every optional Double that is not a finite number (distance, pace, cadence, altitude, alpha1, METs) set to nil; offset, heart rate and power unchanged.
Returns the value when it is a finite number, else nil (nil stays nil).
An Int wrist-HR marker's backup order key is the value itself.
